                         Autolevel Abort/ Fault Report

│ (****************************************************************************)
│ (* The auto level sequence can be aborted in several ways.                  *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (* If the level sequence is active, and the request to begin has already    *)
│ (* occurred, abort the levelling cycle if the level pushbutton is pressed   *)
│ (* again.                                                                   *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (* If the permissive is lost or the watchdog timer times out, abort the     *)
│ (* cycle.                                                                   *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (* If Separating force is detected and the rolls are not turning.           *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (* If the screwdown board tells us the level is no longer active, abort.    *)
│ (* This abort can happen at any time during the level cycle.                *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (* If the drive enable/acknowledge is lost at anytime abort the sequence.   *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (* The auto level abort is disabled when the level cycle is idle.           *)
│ (****************************************************************************)
│

                                 Display Driver

│ (****************************************************************************)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (*  The Display Board will display negative numbers, so we check to         *)
│ (*  see if the value in the Global data register is negative. If it is      *)
│ (*  then we get it's absolute value which is done by subtracting it from    *)
│ (*  zero. Then set an internal bit indicating a negative number will be     *)
│ (*  displayed.                                                              *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (****************************************************************************)
│
│ << RUNG 4  STEP #0002 >>    Cross reference for %M3489
│                             -] [- 10,14
│

│                                                                        Display
│                                                                        Negatve
│                                                                        Number
│ALW_ON
│%S0007  ┌─────┐                                                         %M3489
├──┤ ├───┤ LT_ │                ┌──────────────────────────────────────────( )──
│        │ INT │                │
│        │     │                │
│Global  │     │                │
│Display │     │                │

                   Fault Finder Logic - Screen Type Selection

│ (****************************************************************************)
│ (* This is the beginning of the Fault Finder routine.                       *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (* Fault finder uses three basic groups of registers. They are Faults,      *)
│ (* First Faults, and Unacknowledge.  Each group uses 12 registers.          *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (* R01-12 [Faults] -- Contain the current status of each fault.             *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (* R13-24 [1st Faults] -- First faults that have occurred for each screen.  *)
│ (* First faults are not used by status screens.                             *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (* R25-36 [Unacks] -- Unacknowledged faults.  Whenever a fault occurs,      *)
│ (* it is ORed into this area.  Cleared by the operator by using the F7      *)
│ (* key on the AT computer.  This does not apply to status screens.          *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (* First six control bits determine the type of screen, Fault or Status.    *)
│ (****************************************************************************)
│

│ (****************************************************************************)
│ (* FFACKA determines when all faults are acknowledged.                      *)
│ (* This is typically from one or more of the following sources:             *)
│ (*   - First PLC scan                                                       *)
│ (*   - Mill run one-shot (auto acknowledge)                                 *)
│ (*   - An operator pushbutton                                               *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (* Each screen is individually acknowledged by copying the AT data          *)
│ (* transfer area acknowledge bits to the fault finder's working bits.       *)
│ (****************************************************************************)
│

│OneShot│
│       │
│%M0488 │
├──┤ ├──┘
│
│ << RUNG 12  STEP #0018 >>
│
│ALW_ON
│%S0007  ┌─────┐
├──┤ ├───┤MOVE_├─

│ (*  ********** Inc / Dec / Bounds Check Routine                             *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (*  * IDBUse30.inc ******************************************************   *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (*  This routine performs the following functions:                          *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (*    1. Decrements or increments input value by 1, 10, or a user defined   *)
│ (*       amount.  This is controlled by flags in the input table.           *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (*    2. Bounds checks input value against a minimum and maximum value      *)
│ (*       in the input table.  Result will be greater than or equal to       *)
│ (*       minimum and less than or equal to maximum limits.                  *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (*    3. Sets underflow or overflow flags in result table.                  *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (*    4. Returns validated result and flags to input table for use by main  *)
│ (*       program.                                                           *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (*  *********************************************************************** *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (*  Local Working Register Usage: (Passed to this routine by the caller)    *)
│ (*  =============================                                           *)
│ (*  Note: Because the 90/30 does not have local registers(%L) a group of    *)
│ (*        %R registers must be assigned and act like locals to this routine *)
│ (* .                                                                        *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (* 
           <---------- 16-Bits ----------->                             *)
│ (*           +--------------------------------+                             *)
│ (*   %R0401  | IDB.VAL                        | RETURNED to caller          *)
│ (*           |   Input / Output Value         | (to be modified / tested)   *)
│ (*           +--------------------------------+                             *)
│ (*   %R0402  | IDB.MIN                        |                             *)
│ (*           |   Minimum limit                | value will be >= IDB_MIN    *)
│ (*           +--------------------------------+                             *)
│ (*   %R0403  | IDB.MAX                        |                             *)
│ (*           |   Maximum limit                | value will be <= IDB_MAX    *)
│ (*           +--------------------------------+                             *)
│ (*   %R0404  | IDB.ADD                        |                             *)
│ (*           |   Amount to Add or Subtract    | 1, 10, or passed adder      *)

│ (*            <---------- 16-Bits ----------->                              *)

05-27-26  09:24     GE FANUC SERIES 90-30/90-20/MICRO (v9.05)         Page   422
                                USS01 90-30 PLC
                          Passline Wedge Control Block

│ (****************************************************************************)
│ (* PLine.inc                                                                *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (*    Passline / Wedge                                                      *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (*    On some systems the mill pass line can be adjusted by opening or      *)
│ (*    closing a wedge that moves the roll stack.                            *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (*    Open means the roll gap gets larger and close means the roll gap      *)
│ (*    gets smaller.                                                         *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (*    The operator needs to know the current pass line in order to set it.  *)
│ (*    Based on the wedge position, the calibration settings, and the roll   *)
│ (*    diameters, the passline position can be displayed.                    *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (*    Required hardware / signals:                                          *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (*      - A position transducer to determine the wedge position.            *)
│ (*      - A display to show the current pass line.                          *)
│ (*      - A full open detection device.                                     *)
│ (*      - Manual control to open and close the wedge.                       *)
│ (*      - A means to enter the backup roll and work roll diameters.         *)
│ (*      - A calibration screen to assist the calibration procedure.         *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (*    How it works:                                                         *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (*      The position transducer detects the horizontal position of the      *)
│ (*      wedge.  This position must be translated into a vertical distance   *)
│ (*      traveled by the roll stack.                                         *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (*       - The operator must make sure the backup roll and work roll        *)
│ (*         diameters are correctly entered in the system.                   *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (*       - The operator starts the calibration procedure.                   *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (*       - The wedge must be moved to the full open position.               *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (*       - The transducer is read at this full open position. (PLXOPEN).    *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (*       - The full open position should be marked for vertical measuring.  *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (*       - The wedge must be manually closed until the wedge side work      *)
│ (*         roll is brought to passline.                                     *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (*       - The transducer is read again when at passline. (PLXSPAN).        *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (*       - The vertical distance traveled from full open to passline must   *)
│ (*         be measured and entered into the system. (PLYSPAN).              *)
│ (*                                                                          *)

Program: TEMPER             C:\LM90\TEMPER              Block: PLINE(SUBR 23)
05-27-26  09:24     GE FANUC SERIES 90-30/90-20/MICRO (v9.05)         Page   423
                                USS01 90-30 PLC
                          Passline Wedge Control Block

│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (*    The control system knows these values:                                *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (*          PLXOPEN  feedback at full open position                         *)
│ (*          PLXSPAN  feedback from full open to passline                    *)
│ (*          PLYSPAN  distance traveled from full open to pass line          *)
│ (*          BUDDIAL  wedge side backup roll diameter                        *)
│ (*          WKBDIAL  wedge side work roll diameter                          *)
│ (*          PLWDGPO  current feedback of the position transducer            *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (*         The following Double integer values are calculated:              *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (*          PLCUSKL - current stack value                                   *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (*          PLCAPLL - calibrated passline value                             *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (*          PLCUPLL - current passline value                                *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (*           PLDSPL - passline display value                                *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (*   - The current pass line is then given by:                              *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (*   PLDSPL = PLCUPLL - PLCAPLL                                             *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (*  PLCUPLL = (((PLWDGPO-PLXMIN)*PLYSPAN)/PLXSPAN)+((BUDDIAL/2)+WKBDIAL))   *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (*  PLCAPLL = PLYSPAN + ((BUDDIAL/2)+WKBDIAL))                              *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (*          For simplicity sake the equation is broken down as follows:     *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (*          1> PLXSPAN = PLWDGPO - PLXOPEN                                  *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (*          2> PLWDGEU = ((PLWDGPO-PLXOPEN)*PLYSPAN)/PLXSPAN                *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (*          3> PLCUSKL = (BUDDIAL/2)+WKBDIAL                                *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (*          4> PLCAPPL = PLYSPAN + PLCUSKL                                  *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (*          5> PLCUPLL = PLWDGEU + PLCUSKL                                  *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (*          6> Current pass line                                            *)
│ (*             PASSLN =  PLCUPLL - PLCAPLL                                  *)
│ (*                                                                          *)
│ (*    Note: once PLXOPEN, PLXSPAN, PLYSPAN and PLCUSKL are calculated       *)
│ (*          they are stored by the control system.  These Values used       *)
│ (*          for the current pass line calibration come from the control     *)

Program: TEMPER             C:\LM90\TEMPER              Block: PLINE(SUBR 23)
05-27-26  09:24     GE FANUC SERIES 90-30/90-20/MICRO (v9.05)         Page   424
